newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela mulls minimum wage of $129 or $157/month.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela mulls minimum wage of $129 or $157/month.

text.p: The Venezuelan may raise the minimum wage to either 62,000 bolivars ($129) per month or 75,000 bolivars ($157) but has not yet decided which it will be, said Armando Leon, Vice Planning Minister.
The current urban minimum wage stands at 53,000 bolivars, of which 15,000 bolivars is considered salary and the rest bonuses. The monthly food basket for a family of five costs some 113,000 bolivars.

"Various scenarios have been studied ... but no decision has yet been taken... what we want is for the new level to have as little an inflationary impact as possible," Leon told reporters after leaving the weekly economic cabinet meeting.
Venezuela's largest trade union, the Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV) has asked for a new minimum wage of 90,000 bolivars. Business chamber Fedecamaras has meanwhile suggested 62,000.
The government must announce a final decision after a complex severance reform pay bill, due to go to Congress for discussion Monday, is passed.

At a seminar on Thursday, Toro Hardy, director of state oil company PdVSA, said that according to his own calculations raising the minimum wage to 75,000 bolivars would boost year-end inflation by between six and seven percent.
Venezuela's official 1997 inflation target remains 35 percent.
